selinux_mode.description: SELinux enforcement mode. Use `enforcing` for strict security, `permissive` for logging without blocking, or `disabled` to turn off SELinux entirely. For containers, `permissive` is often used during deployment, but `enforcing` is preferred in production.

selinux_policy_type.description: SELinux policy type. `targeted` restricts only specific daemons/services (recommended for containers); `mls` provides Multi-Level Security (for high-security environments); `minimum` is a stripped-down targeted policy.

selinux_booleans.description: List of SELinux booleans to persistently enable/disable for container compatibility. Each entry must be a fully-qualified `setsebool -P` command string (e.g., `setsebool -P container_manage_cgroup on`).

items.description: A `setsebool -P <bool_name> <on|off>` command line for persistent boolean setting.
